title: When wanting keeps multiplying
issueStatement: You keep feeding appetite, but the appetite is not getting smaller.
centralInsight: Gurbani names greed bluntly because greed colonizes speech, attention, and even spirituality if it is not exposed.
practicalReflection: The issue is not possession alone. It is the kind of wanting that leaves no room for Naam to dwell.
actionPrompt: Notice one appetite you keep obeying automatically. Practice one concrete refusal today.

source.shortMeaning: Greed degrades speech and crowds out the dwelling of Naam.
source.lifeApplication: Do not treat appetite as a harmless private preference.

excerpts.explanation: The diagnosis is severe because the damage is severe.

source.shortMeaning: Wanting needs a new object: what can actually go with you.
source.lifeApplication: Re-aim appetite instead of pretending you have none.

excerpts.explanation: Guru redirects desire instead of merely shaming it.

source.shortMeaning: Freedom can be seen where greed and praise lose their binding power.
source.lifeApplication: Steadiness becomes visible when appetite stops dictating identity.

excerpts.explanation: This excerpt shows the other side of greed: real freedom.
